sections.description: This section provides the essential background on HNF1A-MODY, explaining the transcriptional role of HNF1A in beta-cell function, the specific genetic defect leading to glycosuria, and the implications for insulin secretion and SGLT2 regulation relevant to this patient's presentation.
subtopics: Overview of Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) and autosomal dominant inheritance
HNF1A gene structure, protein function, and its regulatory role in pancreatic beta-cells
Mechanism of insulin/GLUT2 gene dysregulation caused by HNF1A mutations
Clinical distinct features of HNF1A-MODY: glycosuria and beta-cell function profiles
Impact of HNF1A dysfunction on renal glucose reabsorption (SGLT2) and SGLT2 inhibitor risks

sections.description: This segment guides the reader through the clinical recognition process, analyzing how to distinguish this patient's presentation from Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes using family history, biochemical markers, and autoantibody testing results described in the case.
subtopics: Interpreting Family History Patterns: Vertical transmission and early-onset diabetes families
Initial Assessment: Differentiating Autoimmune vs. Genetic Diabetes based on presentation
Role of Autoantibodies (GADA, IA-2A, ZnT8) in ruling out Type 1 Diabetes
Analysis of Glucagon Stimulation Test: Interpreting residual beta-cell function
Evaluation of Clinical Symptoms: Polydipsia, Polyuria, Autonomic dysfunction (Sudoscan), and BMI implications

sections.description: This section details the diagnostic confirmation process, focusing on Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) results, ACMG variant classification pathways, and the specific interpretation of the novel p.N270S mutation found in the patient.
subtopics: Indications for Genetic Testing in young-onset diabetes and the MODY Calculator limitations
Process of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) panels for monogenic diabetes
Case-specific Genetic Finding: The Novel c.809A>G, p.N270S HNF1A mutation
Application of ACMG Guidelines for Pathogenicity Classification of novel variants
Evaluating Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS) and the role of segregation data

sections.description: This part explains the therapeutic strategy shift observed in the case, contrasting initial empiric diabetes management with genotype-driven treatment, and justifying the selection of GLP-1 agonists over insulin or SGLT2 inhibitors.
subtopics: Initial Empiric Treatment and the pitfalls of starting basal insulin in potential MODY cases
Rationale for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Dulaglutide) as first-line therapy for HNF1A-MODY
Comparison of treatment options: Sulfonylureas vs. Insulin vs. GLP-1 vs. DPP-4 inhibitors
Clinical Reasoning for Susceptibility Reduction: Avoiding SGLT2 inhibitors in HNF1A-MODY
Step-down approach in maintenance therapy based on HbA1c control trajectories
